step1_analysis.description: A voltage reference circuit designed to operate based on threshold voltage differences (work function differences) between transistor pairs. The extracted netlist forms a self-biased loop (XM2, XM5), though in this standard CMOS mapping it lacks the specialized depletion/native devices originally used to generate the reference voltage.

paper_reference.title: CMOS Voltage Reference Based on Gate Work Function Differences in Poly-Si Controlled by Conductivity Type and Impurity Concentration

Vref.description: Output reference voltage at room temperature

sky130_expected.calculation: Without the delta-Vth from differently doped poly-Si gates, the loop will likely settle near 0V or a deep subthreshold equilibrium determined by leakage.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard identical NMOS devices cannot produce the intended work-function based reference voltage, resulting in a near-zero or leakage-dependent output.

TC.description: Temperature coefficient of the reference voltage

sky130_expected.calculation: Sweep temperature from -40C to 125C, measure (Vref_max - Vref_min) / 165.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Without the complementary temperature coefficients of the specialized transistors, the TC will not be compensated and will follow standard subthreshold Vth variation, or be near zero if the circuit remains off.

Line_Regulation.description: Variation of the reference voltage with supply voltage changes

sky130_expected.calculation: Sweep VDD from 1.0V to 2.0V, measure delta Vref / delta VDD.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Self-biased loops typically exhibit good line regulation, though in this uncompensated state it will depend heavily on DIBL and leakage.

Power.description: Total power consumption of the reference circuit

sky130_expected.reasoning: Given the lack of a strong pull-up (XM1 has Vgs=0), the circuit will draw only leakage current in a standard CMOS process.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, Temperature Coefficient, Line Regulation, and Power for the voltage reference.
step3_testbench.spice:
* CMOS Voltage Reference Testbench
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

* Parameterized W/L
.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 VDD N0 N0 N0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N0 V1 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VDD V2 GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM5 VDD N0 V1 V1 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}

* Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VV2 V2 0 0

.control
  * 1. DC Operating Point & Power
  op
  let vref = v(V1)
  let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
  print vref power

  * 2. Temperature Sweep for TC
  dc temp -40 125 1
  meas dc vref_max max v(V1)
  meas dc vref_min min v(V1)
  let tc = (vref_max - vref_min) / 165
  print tc

  * 3. VDD Sweep for Line Regulation
  dc VVDD 1.0 2.0 0.1
  meas dc vref_vdd_max max v(V1)
  meas dc vref_vdd_min min v(V1)
  let line_reg = (vref_vdd_max - vref_vdd_min) / 1.0
  print line_reg

  quit
.endc
.end
